kai: Noticed a regression after 0.9.0 where our ingestion workers stall intermittently. Suspect interaction between retry/backoff and aiohttp connector keepalive.

priya: Can you describe stall? Hanging requests or slow starts?

kai: Hanging. Tasks wait on socket acquire, eventually time out. fuser shows sockets in CLOSE_WAIT. We also see repeated auth refresh churn (401 -> refresh -> retry) which might be opening new sessions.

eds: Do you reuse the same AsyncClient across retries? We introduced a retry wrapper that calls `await client._request(...)` directly and sometimes recreates a session on token refresh. That could break connector reuse.

kai: We *do* have a token refresh hook that recreates session to reload headers. Maybe that was harmless before. Repro snippet:```py
async def _maybe_refresh(c):
    if token_expired():
        c._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(headers=new_headers)

async def worker(c):
    for _ in range(1000):
        await c.generate('x')
```

rachel: Oof. Replacing the session object while async requests are in flight will leak connectors. Instead update auth headers on the connector or use `ClientSession._default_headers.update(...)` (private but avoids teardown). Better: expose `update_headers()` on AsyncClient that swaps headers atomically.

kai: Agreed. Also noticed typing doesn't help here since AsyncClient hides `_session` internals and many methods annotated as Any. Hard to discover that code recreates session.

priya: Proposal: 1) add public `rotate_credentials()` coroutine on AsyncClient that refreshes auth without recreating session; 2) ensure internal use of `aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=DEFAULT_CONN_LIMIT, enable_cleanup_closed=True)`; 3) add type signatures for internal session attr as Optional[ClientSession] and export types in py.typed.

eds: I can own a PR for rotate_credentials + docs. For the connector we should also allow `max_connections` config and default to min(100, cpu_count*25). Also add an option `reuse_sessions_on_retry: bool` default True.

ci-bot: Created ticket #812: add rotate_credentials and connection pool controls to python-sdk.

rachel: One more: retries currently do exponential backoff but don't respect `ConnectionError` vs 500. We should avoid retrying on auth 401 and prefer immediate refresh+single retry. That will reduce session churn.

kai: For mitigation I switched to short-lived clients per batch and saw reduced hangs, but throughput dropped ~20%. Need long-lived client pattern documented.

priya: Let's add a small sample app to docs showing: create AsyncClient once, call `await client.rotate_credentials()` on refresh, and use `asyncio.Semaphore(200)` for in-flight calls. Also include typed example with `from redwood.client import AsyncClient, AsyncClientType` so IDE shows available methods.

eds: I'll add unit tests: assert that after 5000 quick rotates open sockets remain stable, and typing check with mypy in CI.

kai: Thanks. Can someone add a note to the migration guide for 0.9.1 so users don't recreate sessions on token refresh?

priya: Will do. I'll also add a runtime debug message when someone assigns to `.session` or calls `.close()` incorrectly so it's easier to catch in logs.

ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1288 (rotate credentials + pool opts + types).

rachel: Nice. Also add a deprecation warning for using private `_session` attr.

kai: Perfect. Follow-up: can we also add a small benchmark in examples/ showing throughput vs concurrency when using semaphore vs connector limit? That was useful earlier.

eds: Adding that to the PR. Will ping when green.

kai: Great, thanks all :rocket:
